better page».

**What the data said.** D-281 gave the query to the article «Verneombudets rolle i det psykososiale arbeidsmiljøet»
(/artikler/verneombudets-rolle-i-kartleggingen): its title and H1 carried the words. Google shows /verneombud for the
query anyway — the page every header and footer links, with a FAQ — so two of our pages competed and the one shown
did not answer the question in its title, H1 or first line. The results page (OpenSEO, Norway, bokmål) is guides to
the safety representative's role, duties and rights in the psychosocial environment — Arbeidstilsynet, NHO, the
unions, two HSE portals — not survey pages. The demand is the role, not the mapping: «verneombud» about 3 600 searches
a month, «verneombud oppgaver» 880, «verneombudets rolle» 170, the exact phrase about 50. A page at 60 on 25
impressions is a page problem before it is an authority problem.

**What changed.** The pages were separated rather than merged (the strategy's phase-2 note considered both):
- **/verneombud is the guide to the cluster.** Title «Verneombud og psykososialt arbeidsmiljø: oppgaver | Orgpuls»,
  H1 «Hva er verneombudets rolle i det psykososiale arbeidsmiljøet?», a lead that answers it in the first sentence
  with aml § 6-2, and the card and description to match. New sections, every heading a question: what the law says
  (the law block gains aml § 6-5 on training, time and pay); six duties as cards (follow, raise, take part in the
  mapping, in the risk assessment, be consulted on measures, go further); six rights as a list (training of at least
  40 hours that covers the psychosocial environment — forskrift om organisering, ledelse og medvirkning §§ 3-18 and
  3-19; time; information, § 6-2 fifth paragraph; to be consulted; to stop dangerous work, § 6-3; to take part in an
  inspection); what changed in 2024 (safety representative from five employees, committee from 30, aml §§ 6-1 and
  7-1) and 2026 (chapter 1A: mapping with the representatives, §§ 1A-2 and 1A-4); bullying, conflict and harassment
  (aml §§ 4-3, 2 A-2 and 2 A-4 — the representative sees that the employer acts, and does not investigate); and the
  sections it had (the five steps, what to see, raising it, when management does not act, the small department).
  FAQ from six to ten: the role first, then training, whether the representative can demand a mapping, and
  representative versus union steward. The 2024 thresholds are confirmed on Arbeidstilsynet's pages; the year the
  psychosocial duty entered § 6-2 is not, so the page does not date it.
- **The article narrows to the survey.** Title «Verneombudets rolle når arbeidsmiljøet kartlegges | Orgpuls»; its
  second paragraph points to /verneombud for the role as a whole. The English title already said «role in
  psychosocial mapping».
- **Nine inbound links carrying the page's words**: «verneombud og psykososialt arbeidsmiljø» from /lovkrav and the
  articles on the mapping requirement, the 2026 rules, the safety round, the working-environment mapping and «is it
  required?»; «verneombudets rolle i det psykososiale arbeidsmiljøet» from the hub /psykososialt-arbeidsmiljo (its
  anchor relinked from «rettigheter og plikter»), the employee-survey article and the kartlegging article itself —
  each a sentence in the paragraph where the representative is already named (D-235: articles link pages of the law
  and the role, not the product's).
- **Sweden's /skyddsombud** is extended to the same shape — the Swedish pack must match every array's length — under
  Swedish law: AML 6 kap. 4 § (training as a joint duty, no hour count), 5 § (leave with benefits), 6 §, 6 a §, 7 §
  (stopping work), 10 § (protection); AFS 2023:1 5, 6, 11 and 13 §§; AFS 2023:2 2 kap. 4, 10 and 11 §§;
  diskrimineringslagen 2 kap. 3 §; MBL 11 §. Its timeline is 2016 (AFS 2015:4) and 2025 (AFS 2023:1 and 2023:2).
  No article links: Sweden's site serves none. The United Kingdom's /safety-representatives is unchanged — its pack
  holds its own page under its own law.
- **The keyword map** (`tests/unit/seo-geo.test.ts`) pins the new split: the query and «verneombudets rolle» on
  /verneombud's title and H1, «rettigheter og plikter» on its description, «verneombudets rolle i kartleggingen» on
  the article. Strategy § 4 rows and the phase-2 note are rewritten accordingly.

**Not done, and why.** OpenSEO's Search Console is not connected, so the only ranking data is Sentral's panel; the
connection is a click in the project's search-performance page and would give query-level impressions per page. The
Sentral mapping stays /verneombud. The effect is read in four to six weeks: the query's position, and whether
/verneombud or the article is shown for it.

## D-289 — German is a platform language and Germany a market: the app in German with English behind it, market `de` with the USt-IdNr. (2026-10-29)

Tor, 29 October 2026: «lives at de.orgpuls.com, start building it» (X-115). DE-A and DE-B in docs/markets/PLAN.md
phase 3, on Sweden's pattern (D-252, D-254, D-255). Nothing changes for Norway, Sweden or the United Kingdom, and
de.orgpuls.com still answers as D-258 says until DE-F.

1. **The registry** (`lib/i18n/locales.ts`) makes `de` a platform language with English as its fallback, so a text
   not yet in German is shown in English, never as a key. It is not a survey language yet (`survey: false`,
   `surveyTexts: 'registry'`): the statements, the respondent pages and the invitation texts are DE-A2, drafted
   into the translation registry as the other survey languages were (X-071, X-089). The `Locale` type widens with
   it, so the account menu offers Deutsch and the company form's chip knows it.
2. **`messages/de.json`** holds the app's chrome: 3 278 strings in 41 namespaces, exactly the keys `sv.json`
   carries, machine drafts following `docs/translations/de.md` for Tor to review — Sie-form, gender-neutral role
   nouns (Beschäftigte, Führungskraft, Geschäftsführung, Abteilungsleitung, Sicherheitsbeauftragte), German
   typography („…“ and the spaced en dash where the source has « » and —).
   - **Left out on purpose**, as for Swedish: `respond`, `mail` and the registry-owned factor and extra fields
     (DE-A2); `site` and `seo` (the German site is written for German law, DE-F); `dpa` (DE-E); `industry`
     (Norwegian industry names, which `contentLang` shows a German reader in English).
   - **Norwegian law stays Norwegian.** The help articles and the header panel's law tab describe
     arbeidsmiljøloven, named as such, with Arbeidstilsynet as «Arbeitsaufsichtsbehörde» and Enhetsregisteret and
     Brønnøysund by name: a German-speaking leader of a Norwegian organisation reads about Norwegian law in German.
     A German organisation's own legal texts are DE-C, laid over the catalogue by host.
3. **The language chip** in Oppsett › Selskap printed bokmål, English and otherwise «Svenska», so a fourth
   language would have been labelled Svenska. It is now a table keyed by platform language
   (`components/oppsett/CompanyForm.tsx`), where a missing label is a type error, with
   `oppsett.companySettings.langDe` in all four catalogues.
4. **The database** (0235) adds `de` to the four lists of platform languages: `organizations.default_lang`,
   `profiles.lang`, `demo_requests.lang` and `markets.default_lang`. The employee register's survey languages
   (`employees_language_check`, the dispatcher's `LANGS`) are unchanged until DE-A2. `tests/unit/locales.test.ts`
   holds each list to the registry.
5. **Market `de`** (0236): floor 5, German, Europe/Berlin, organisation-number rule `de_ustid`. The
   Umsatzsteuer-Identifikationsnummer is the one identifier every trading German business has that is national,
   unique and checkable: the Handelsregister number is per court and not unique nationally, and a sole trader has
   none (`docs/markets/de-legal.md`, assumptions). Its shape is DE plus nine digits, the ninth an ISO 7064 MOD 11,10
   check digit over the first eight (`app.de_ustid_check`); a small business under § 19 UStG may have none, so the
   number stays optional at sign-up as in every market. The trigger holds a German organisation's number to the
   rule; `lib/org-number.ts` is the same rule at the form, accepts «DE 136 695 976» and lower case, and prints
   «DE 136 695 976»; a refused number gets `registrer.problem.invalid_org_number_de` in the four catalogues. No
   register is asked (`REGISTRY_LOOKUP`): the sign-up confirms the typed name, as Sweden's does.
6. **The German legal pack** (`lib/legal/pack.ts` `GERMANY`) is a shell until DE-C: no duty threshold for a safety
   representative (German law elects a Betriebsrat, it does not require one), a committee from 21 employees
   (§ 11 ASiG, the Arbeitsschutzausschuss in firms with more than twenty), no industry list for an occupational
   health service, and empty provisions, coverage, gaps and factor references. `LEGAL_PACK.de` is false, so no
   market pack is laid over the catalogue yet.
7. **Mail and SMS** (`supabase/functions/_shared/mail.ts`, `sms.ts`): brand Orgpuls, time zone Europe/Berlin. An
   organisation in German reads English, as a Swedish one does (D-255), until the leaders' notices exist in German
   (`orgLangOf`, `groupLang`). The survey's own language in Germany is English: `surveyBaseOf` now takes the first
   of the market's languages the survey has (`de` → `en` today), mirrored in `MARKET_SURVEY_BASE`, so DE-A2 makes
   it German with no change here. A German mobile number (015x–017x) is normalised to +49 for SMS.
8. **Not a site yet.** `lib/hosts.ts` is unchanged, so de.orgpuls.com still redirects to the English site and no
   organisation can join market `de` before DE-F. `DPA_MARKET.de` and `PRICE_MARKET.de` point at Norway's agreement
   and prices until DE-E; `MARKET_BRAND.de` is orgpuls; `PACK_LANGS.de` is empty.

Tests:
- `supabase/tests/markets_invariants.sql` rows 25–26: the German row, and the rule on DE136695976 and DE811569869,
  a wrong check digit, a bare nine digits, a lower-case prefix, an Austrian number and a Norwegian number, with the
  check function's digits.
- `tests/unit/german-platform.test.ts`: the registry and the fallback; key parity with bokmål and with Swedish; the
  registry-owned namespaces and fields out; German typography; a chip label for every platform language; the
  market's languages.
- `tests/unit/markets.test.ts`, `org-number.test.ts`, `sms.test.ts`, `mail.test.ts`, `p1-language.test.ts`,
  `locales.test.ts`, `swedish-platform.test.ts` as before, with the German cases added.

**Seen in the browser** (QA stack, Kari the daglig leder, cookie `de`): Innsikt, Resultater, Målinger, Tiltak,
Rapport, Kommentarer, Oppsett, Hjelp, Måleoppsett, Integrasjoner and the Slack, SMS, Teams and Entra pages render
with `lang="de"`, German headings, no raw key, no `undefined` or `NaN`, and no console error; at 390 px Innsikt and
Oppsett have no horizontal scroll. The heatmap's column for motstrid was too wide as «Widerspruch» and is «Konflikt», and the
threshold tile on Oppsett clipped «Mindestgruppengröße» at 390 px, so that one label is «Mindestgröße».
**Gap, as D-252's:** factor names and statements in a German leader's results show in English, because the
registry overlay (D-253) lays only a language whose survey texts are approved — DE-A2.

**Hosted:** 0235 and 0236 are **not applied** — the Supabase connector in this session is not authenticated, so
`apply_migration` is not available to it. The code works against the old schema meanwhile: the language switch's
profile save of «Deutsch» fails silently and the cookie keeps the choice on the device; `restoreLocale` likewise;
a demo request from a visitor whose cookie is `de` would be refused by `demo_requests_lang_check` (the site's own
switch offers only the site's languages, so that needs the app's switch first). Apply the two files verbatim
through `apply_migration` before anyone is offered German; the four hosted lists then read `no, en, sv, de`.

**Not yet:** DE-A2, DE-C, DE-E, DE-F and DE-G as PLAN.md phase 3 lists them. The app footer's company line and
Oppsett › Selskap's Norwegian-law blocks (BHT, verneombud, AMU thresholds) for a German organisation are DE-C.

## D-290 — Germany's law in the product: the German legal pack, in German and English (DE-C, 2026-10-29)

DE-C in docs/markets/PLAN.md phase 3 (X-115), on Sweden's and the United Kingdom's pattern (D-257, D-265). An
organisation in market `de` reads German law in German or in English; nothing changes for Norway, Sweden or the
United Kingdom, and a Norwegian organisation's German-speaking leader still reads Norwegian law in German (D-289).

1. **The pack** is `messages/market/de/{de,en}.json`, 227 keys in each: every text that states Norwegian law
   (the 105 keys `tests/unit/legal-pack.test.ts` finds by their words), the two that offer a threshold under the
   market's floor of five, every text that names the third role (58), the two billing texts that named the report
   to Arbeidstilsynet, and a handful the market needs — the USt-IdNr. as the organisation number's label and
   hint, a German mobile number as the example. Written from `docs/markets/de-legal.md`, each citation in the
   German convention («§ 5 Abs. 3 Nr. 6 ArbSchG») in both languages, the acts by their German short names in
   English too.
2. **The third role is «Betriebsrat»** («Works council» in English) for a German organisation: `role.verneombud`
   and every text that names the role are in the pack. The texts say what the law says: a works council is the
   employees' right from five eligible employees (§ 1 BetrVG), never the employer's duty; where there is one, it
   co-determines the method of the risk assessment (§ 87 Abs. 1 Nr. 7 BetrVG), is informed (§ 80 Abs. 2) and
   involved (§ 89 Abs. 2); where there is none, the role stays empty or goes to a person the employees chose. The
   test holds that no text tells a German firm it must have one. No role is added (de-legal.md, assumptions 2).
3. **The structure** (`lib/legal/pack.ts` `GERMANY`): seven provisions — § 5, § 3 and § 6 ArbSchG; §§ 80, 87, 89
   BetrVG; §§ 2, 5, 11 ASiG; §§ 3, 7, 12, 13 AGG; Art. 6(1)(c) GDPR with § 26 BDSG. Eight coverage rows on the
   fields § 4 Nr. 4 ArbSchG names, the mapping the product's own and said so on the screen: Arbeitsinhalt (rolle,
   medvirk, mening), Arbeitsorganisation (mengde, motstrid, kontakt), soziale Beziehungen (leder, kollega, ytring,
   integritet), emotionale Inanspruchnahme (emosjon); Belästigung and Gewalt as screenings; Arbeitsumgebung and
   Arbeitszeit shown as not measured (the German module is DE-D). Five gaps: the rest of the
   Gefährdungsbeurteilung, the Unterweisung, the works agreement on the method, Betriebsarzt and Fachkraft, the AGG
   complaints body. Every factor's reference is «§ 5 Abs. 3 Nr. 6 ArbSchG · …» with the provision closest to what
   it measures. The duties stay as D-289 set them: no representative by headcount, the Arbeitsschutzausschuss from
   more than twenty with no «may» band (§ 11 ASiG), no industry list for the Betriebsarzt (§§ 2, 5 ASiG).
4. **What the texts never say**, and the test holds: no factor name attributed to the statute; nothing «nach der
   GDA» (the guideline was not read, de-legal.md UNVERIFIED 1); no annual interval as if the statute set one
   (§ 3 Abs. 1 ties review to effectiveness and change); no duty on employees to report harassment (Germany has
   no counterpart to aml § 2-3 (2) d); the authority is «die Arbeitsschutzbehörde des Landes», never the
   Berufsgenossenschaft as a rule; the survey «eine standardisierte schriftliche Befragung», never «von der GDA
   empfohlen».
5. **The mail**: the pack's `mail` keys — the works council's advance notice, the results-ready and evaluation
   notices, the measures copy — reach the dispatcher through `scripts/functions/deploy.mjs` as every market's do
   (D-257), in German and English; a German organisation's leaders read the English (D-289) until the leaders'
   notices exist in German.
6. **Still Norway's**: prices, currency and the data processing agreement (DE-E); the public site (DE-F). The
   respondent's own texts are the registry's (DE-A2) and are not in a pack.

Tests: `tests/unit/legal-pack.test.ts` — the generic pack rules now run for `de` (every Norwegian-law text replaced
in both languages, no Norwegian law of its own, every structure key present, nothing a screen does not read, every
factor's reference, the nearest language for a reader of bokmål or Polish), and a Germany block: the duties, the
committee at 20 and 21, no industry list, the shape of every factor reference, no GDA or annual claim, the role
label in both languages and no «must have a works council». `npm run verify:i18n` checks the pack's parity and
ICU arguments (227 keys in de, en).

**Seen in the browser** (QA stack, the QA tenant moved into market `de` with the USt-IdNr. DE 136 695 976 for the
check and moved back after it, Kari the daglig leder, cookies `de` and `en`): the role chip, the duties card and
every screen read «Betriebsrat» / «Works council» and never «Sicherheitsbeauftragte» or «safety representative»;
Oppsett › Rechtsgrundlagen lists the seven provisions, the eight coverage rows with ✓ and ! and the five gaps in
German and in English; Innsikt, Rapport, Måleoppsett, Målinger, Hjelp, the SMS page, Kommentarer and Tiltak carry
the ArbSchG citations and no Norwegian authority, with no raw key and no console error; Oppsett › Selskap labels
the number USt-IdNr. and prints it as DE 136 695 976. **Gap, as D-289's:** the factor names in the coverage rows
and the results are English for a German reader until German is a survey language (DE-A2).

**Not yet:** a German lawyer's review of the pack and of de-legal.md's UNVERIFIED 1–10, the EU-representative
question (UNVERIFIED 7) before DE-G; DE-A2, DE-D, DE-E, DE-F and DE-G as PLAN.md lists them.

## D-291 — Germany's site on de.orgpuls.com, built behind a flag (DE-F, 2026-10-29)

DE-F in docs/markets/PLAN.md phase 3 (X-115), on Sweden's pattern (D-270, D-276): a site of its own for Germany, in
German, for German law, with the product in German or English behind it. It ships closed: `DE_SITE=open`, an
environment variable `lib/hosts.ts` reads once when it loads, puts the site's row into `SITES`; until DE-G sets it
on Vercel, de.orgpuls.com keeps answering as D-258 says (every address to the English site), and nothing on
Norway's, Sweden's or Empvibe's hosts changes. The pack, the pictures, the cards and the tests ship now, so the
switch is one variable.

1. **The host** (`lib/hosts.ts` `DE_SITE`, `DE_PAGES`, `DE_PATHS`): de.orgpuls.com, market `de`, language `de`,
   languages de and en, the ten pages Sweden serves — the start page, the platform, the use cases, why Orgpuls, the
   law, the works council, small businesses, security, contact and the privacy notice — at German addresses
   (`/gefaehrdungsbeurteilung-psychische-belastung`, `/betriebsrat`, `/kleine-unternehmen`, `/sicherheit`,
   `/datenschutz`, `/anwendungsfaelle`, `/warum-orgpuls`, `/anmelden`, `/registrieren`). A Norwegian address
   answers 308 to the German one; a page the site does not serve (prices, terms, industries, articles, templates,
   the demo) and another site's address (`/skyddsombud`) answer 404; sign-in and sign-up are served.
   `RESERVED_HOSTS` names the host while the flag is off, so the gate keeps sending it to the English site. The
   sitemap, robots, llms.txt, the canonical URL and `hreflang="de-DE"` follow from the row as for every site of its
   own; nothing there names a market.
2. **The words** (`messages/market/de/de.json`, now 1 816 keys; `en.json` 320): every page word Sweden's pack
   carries — site.chrome, site.home, site.plattform, site.bruksomrader, site.hvorfor, site.contact, site.story,
   seo.common, seo.signup, seo.og, seo.shots, seo.llms, seo.home, seo.pages.{plattform, bruksomrader, sikkerhet,
   kontakt, personvernerklaering}, seo.lp.{lovkrav, verneombud, smaaBedrifter}, seo.voTip, start — written in
   German from the Swedish, for German law from docs/markets/de-legal.md, with the three chrome keys a site of its
   own has beyond Norway's (nav.kontakt, nav.smaaBedrifter, footer.link.verneombud). English carries the chrome
   (93 keys) for a sign-in or sign-up read in English on the German site, as Sweden's does; the page words are in
   German only, which `scripts/verify/i18n.mjs` `PAGES_IN_SITE_LANG` now allows for `de` as for `se`, since the
   site pins its pages to German (lib/i18n/request.ts, `PAGE_LANG_HEADER`). The gate holds the pack's parity and ICU
   arguments; an array in no.json is an array in the pack. The pack is built, not written by hand: a session
   script lays the flat German and English texts over no.json's key order, refuses a key no.json lacks unless it is
   a structure key or one Sweden's pack owns, checks every ICU signature against the source and shapes arrays as
   the source has them. The start words say no trial and no card (DE-E), as Sweden's.
3. **What the pages say, and `tests/unit/de-site.test.ts` holds** (on se-site's pattern, 17 tests): nothing only
   true in Norway and nothing in Norwegian outside the footer's company line and the privacy notice's facts about
   the provider; no claim German law does not allow — no «zertifiziert», no approval, no survey required by law,
   nothing filed with the authority, no interval as if the statute set one, no duty to have a works council; no
   price, «kostenlos» or trial (DE-E); no threshold under five; not «auf Deutsch» for the survey (DE-A2); no SMS
   outside the privacy notice; every menu and footer entry worded in German and in English; every array as long as
   Norway's. The law page cites §§ 3, 5 and 6 ArbSchG and § 87 Abs. 1 Nr. 7 BetrVG for the four steps, § 21
   Abs. 1a for the inspections from 2026, and §§ 22, 25 and 26 ArbSchG for the ladder (Besichtigung und Beratung,
   Auskunft und Unterlagen, Anordnung, Bußgeld bis 30.000 Euro und Strafe); the works-council page §§ 1, 80, 87,
   89, 37, 40, 78, 23, 84 and 85 BetrVG and § 22 SGB VII; the security page rests the processing on Art. 6 Abs. 1
   lit. c DSGVO and § 26 Abs. 1 BDSG with § 5 ArbSchG as the duty, a Betriebsvereinbarung under § 26 Abs. 4,
   never consent (§ 26 Abs. 2); the privacy notice names the Land's data-protection authority (the
   Bundesbeauftragte's list at bfdi.bund.de) beside Datatilsynet. The provisions this entry cites beyond
   de-legal.md — §§ 13, 22, 25, 26 ArbSchG, §§ 23, 37, 40, 75, 78, 84, 85 BetrVG, §§ 3, 6 ASiG, § 26 BDSG — were
   read from gesetze-im-internet.de in this session (its pages answered the session's WebFetch 503 and curl 200).
   The third role is «Betriebsrat» throughout, and the tip mail is the works council's to the Geschäftsführung.
4. **The pictures** (DE-F3): `scripts/seed/design-fixture.de.mjs` tells the scenario as Nordwind Tiefbau GmbH —
   market de, German, Europe/Berlin, the USt-IdNr. DE999999995 (the check digit `app.de_ustid_check` computes, at
   the far end of the series), id space 8049 — every Norwegian text replaced and the same answers and figures (28
   of 34, index 61, 64 the year before), held by the generator's own checks; `scripts/qa/up.sh` seeds it and
   `supabase/tests/local_account.sql` signs in to it. `product-shots.mjs --market de` takes the nine screens signed
   in as its Geschäftsführerin, in German, on Berlin's clock, into assets/produkt/de; `og-images.mjs --market de`
   draws the cards into public/og/de (the law, the works council, small businesses, default) in German with German
   pills; `lib/marketing/shots.ts` `DE_SHOTS` and `SITE_SHOTS.de` hand them to the site. The questionnaire is in
   English, as a German employee meets it (`locale_de`, DE-A2); the report's factor table names the factors from
   the translation registry, in English for a German organisation until German is approved there (the gap D-289
   names), while the overview and the heatmap name them from the German catalogue. Two defects the pictures
   showed are fixed: the surveys page, the overview, the report, the pulse view, the platform page and the
   invitation page lower-cased a German noun inside a sentence («6 Fragen zu meinungsklima und arbeitsmenge»);
   `lowerInSentence` (lib/i18n/locales.ts) leaves German as it is and lower-cases the other languages as before.

   «§ 5 Abs. 3 Nr. 6 ArbSchG», «Anonym ab 5 Antworten», two rows as Sweden's.
5. **Still Norway's, or waiting**: prices, currency, terms and the DPA (DE-E; the site states no price and links
   no terms); the mail links (`MARKET_SITE_URL.de` joins with DE-G, since tests/unit/market-links.test.ts couples
   the table to `SITES`); the German survey (DE-A2); the German module (DE-D); a German lawyer's reading

Tests: tests/unit/de-site.test.ts; tests/unit/markets.test.ts' Germany block (reserved by default, open with
`DE_SITE`); se-site, legal-pack, market-links, german-platform and plurals unchanged and green; `npm run

audit (nothing new); `node scripts/i18n/page-map.mjs --check` (66 pages match); tsc and lint.

the switch.

## D-292 — German is a survey language: the respondent texts drafted, the database's lists widened, the modules' German by code (DE-A2, 2026-10-29)

Tor, 29 October 2026: «lives at de.orgpuls.com, start building it» (X-115). DE-A2 in docs/markets/PLAN.md phase 3,
on the pattern of the five survey languages before it (D-133, X-071, X-089) and of German as a platform language
(D-289). Nothing is approved here: as for every other survey language, a German text reaches a respondent only once
a person has approved it, and German is offered only where a pilot or the flag says so.

1. **The registry** (`lib/i18n/locales.ts`): `de` is `survey: true`, its respondent texts in the translation registry
   (`surveyTexts: 'registry'`), as Swedish. With that one change every derived list moves: `TRANSLATION_LOCALES` and
   `RESPONDENT_LOCALES`, the dispatcher's `SURVEY_ONLY`, the language picker on the survey page, and `surveyBaseOf('de')`,
   which is German now that the first of the market's languages is a survey language (D-280); `MARKET_SURVEY_BASE.de` is
   German with it, so a German organisation's survey opens in German and its invitation is written in German where it
   is offered, and in English otherwise. `locale_de` joins the flags, not signed off: German is offered by a pilot
   (`locales.pilot`) until Tor approves the texts, as English, Polish and Lithuanian were.
2. **The database** (0237) widens the lists the unit test holds to the registry (`tests/unit/locales.test.ts`): the
   check constraints on `employees.language`, `item_translations.locale`, `ui_translation_approvals.locale` and
   `locale_pilots.locale`, and the functions that name the languages — `app.round_locale_state`,
   `public.dispatch_language_texts`, the platform's `app.op_translations_import`, `op_translations_approve`,
   `op_locale_pilot` and `op_auto_record` (0206's names for 0086's and 0101's bodies), and the Entra sync's
   `public.entra_sync_apply` (0165), so a person whose directory language is German keeps it. Each is the repository's
   latest definition with `de` added and nothing else changed: generated from the migration texts and proved on the
   local stack by diffing `pg_get_functiondef` before and after — two lines per function, four for the dispatcher's.
   No destructive statement. The test now also holds `op_auto_record`, `entra_sync_apply`, and the literal lists in
   `supabase/functions/_shared/mail.ts` (`Lang`, `LANGS`, `DATE_LOCALE`) and `entra.ts` (`LANGS`) to the registry.
3. **The product's own texts, 212**, drafted by machine into `docs/translations/de.orgpuls-translations.json`
   (`orgpuls-translations` v1, locale `de`, origin *machine*, step *draft*): the 33 core statements, the 23 texts of the
   questions outside the index, the 111 strings of the survey pages, the 45 invitation, reminder and SMS texts. Written
   following `docs/translations/de.md`, whose new section «The survey in German» has the scales, the terms and the
   open questions: Sie-form; the agreement scale «Stimme gar nicht zu / Stimme eher nicht zu / Weder noch / Stimme eher
   zu / Stimme voll zu»; «Trifft auf mich nicht zu»; «Keine Angabe»; the round names without an article
   («Basisbefragung {year}», «Pulsbefragung {n} · {year}») so «zur {round}» and «Die {round} endet morgen» stay
   grammatical; «Ihre Führungskraft» for the leader and as the `{name}` fallback, «die Leitung» for ledelsen,
   «Geschäftsführung» in the invitation's signature, «Arbeitnehmervertretung» in the thank-you text. The package passes
   `checkImport` as the platform's import runs it — 212 rows, zero errors and zero warnings, so every row was made from
   the current bokmål — and the four SMS texts stay one GSM-7 message each. It is written as a package for the platform's
   `translations.import` because this repository cannot write to the hosted registry; proved locally through
   `app.op_translations_import('de', …)` with a platform actor: 817 new rows, none refused, on the first try.
4. **The seven published modules' texts, 605, by code with each module.** A module text's registry key is its
   item's uuid (`module:<uuid>`), which differs between databases: the local rebuild during this work regenerated every
   id, and the first package, keyed by the old ones, matched nothing. So the modules' German ships as
   `modules/<key>/registry/de.json` (D-263), keyed by the module file's own codes, for all seven modules — HSE 218,
   Arbetstid och återhämtning 28, Bygg og anlegg 48, Helse og omsorg 49, Handel 49, Barnehage og skole 102,
   Kunnskap og kontor 103 — which `npm run -s modules:registry` resolves against the database it runs on, hashed on the
   bokmål each translates (D-253). The registry-file format (`lib/modules/registry-file.ts`) grew what the five modules
   without files needed and the two with files did not: `segments` (a segment question is an item coded
   `<prefix>-S-<id>`, 0090), and for a worded module (0083) `variants` and `factorVariants`, the kindergarten and school
   wording of a text and of a factor name, written as `module:<id>:v:<wording>` and `mfactor:<id>:v:<wording>` on the
   bokmål wording's hash, exactly as the catalogue keys them. Resolved on the local stack: 597 rows, Barnehage's 54
   wordings among them; kunnskap's file names 15 factors where that database holds 23, eight being leftovers of an
   earlier file that no module names. The five Norwegian and British modules carry only German in their registry folder:
   their other languages were imported as packages before the folder existed, and stay in the hosted registry.
5. **The employee import** (`app/(app)/oppsett/actions.ts` `languageOf`) read a language column of bokmål, English,
   Polish and Lithuanian only, so a Swede or a Dane imported by spreadsheet could not be marked. It is now one table over
   every survey language — code, bokmål name, English name, own name (`de`, `deutsch`, `tysk`, `german`) — and a
   language added to the registry without its words is a type error, as the language chip is (D-289). German is
   stored only once `locale_de` is on, so the code works against a hosted register that predates 0237 (the playbook's
   expand-before-contract); the flag is signed off after the texts are approved, which needs 0237 anyway, and a German
   organisation's employees meet German through the organisation's language meanwhile.
6. **CI** seeds the German fixture (`--market de`) as it seeds the British and the Swedish, which D-291 left to
   `scripts/qa/up.sh` alone. The SQL probes that used `de` as a language the database refuses (`locale_pilot_invariants`
   row 2, `legal_invariants` row 4) use Finnish; `survey_language_invariants` row 2 inserts a German text and a German
   employee beside the Swedish and Danish ones.

**Gates:** tsc 0, lint 0, verify:i18n PASS, `npx vitest run` 85 files / 1 060 tests, `npm run -s modules:validate`,
`npm run qa:up -- --reset` then `npm run test:db` (101 suites), `node scripts/audit/wiring.mjs` 0 findings,
`NEXT_DIST_DIR=.next-build npx next build` exit 0.

**Tests:** `tests/unit/german-survey.test.ts` (15): the registry row and every derived list; the flag present and not
signed off; the package exactly the catalogue of the product's texts, every entry a machine draft, `checkImport` with
no problem; typography (Sie, „…“, the spaced en dash, no GDA, no stray space) and GSM-7 for the SMS texts; each of the
seven registry files complete against its module's definition (factors, statements, count questions and their options,
segments, wordings, scales and prefaces where the module has them), a translation and not the bokmål, and no eighth
module with a file. `tests/unit/locales.test.ts` (19) as in 2. `module-hse`, `module-arbetstid`, `module-instrument`,
`entra-sync`, `p1-language`, `dates`, `german-platform` and `mail` follow.

**Seen in the browser** (the QA stack rebuilt with 0237, the package imported through the platform command and, for
the check only, every German row set approved on the local stack): the Lumio survey at `/s/<token>?lang=de` offers
Norsk, English and Deutsch, opens with «Bevor Sie beginnen», carries `lang="de"` on the survey, and walks all eleven
statements in German with «Stimme gar nicht zu … Stimme voll zu», «Trifft auf mich nicht zu», «Möchten Sie mehr sagen?
Freiwillig und anonym», «Zurück», «Überspringen», «Weiter» to «Absenden», at 390 and 320 px, with no raw key, no
bokmål, no console error and nothing wider than the screen. Signed in as Nordwind's Geschäftsführerin, the report's
factor table reads «Meinungsklima», «Rollenklarheit», «Anerkennung und Sinn» from the registry (D-253's overlay, now for
German), where D-291's picture had English; the pictures are retaken once German is approved on the hosted project.

**Not yet (DE-G):** hosted migration 0237 after 0235 and 0236; the package imported through `translations.import` and
`npm run -s modules:registry | psql` against the hosted project; a pilot for the first German organisation, or Tor's
sign-off of `locale_de` after reading the drafts; the German reader's review of the open questions in
`docs/translations/de.md`.

## D-293 — One source for every market: the registry, delta packs, source tracking, every site in CI (2026-10-29)

The owner's question: can a change be made once and reach Sweden, Germany and the UK, so that only the language
differs? The code paths were shared already; the text and the market facts were not. An architecture review
(«Multi-market architecture review», 29 October) found the gaps; this closes them, without a migration.

1. **The market registry** (`lib/markets.ts` `MARKET_CONFIG`). The maps the code kept per market (brand, price
   list, DPA, pack languages, floors, time zones, register lookup, the hosts' brands and default addresses,
   Germany's opening) are read from it; the edge functions' maps (brand name, site, Auth language, mail domain,
   time zone, phone rule, support inbox) are generated from it (`npm run markets:edge`). Components ask it: the
   VAT number in Oppsett › Betaling (`billing.vatNumber`, held to `save_billing`, 0227), the law seal (§ in
   Sweden and Germany, whose law is cited by section; ✓ only in the UK, as D-271 decided for the UK), the
   «Tips ledelsen» utm_source, Plattform's register glyph, and industries and the demo in the menu by the pages
   a site serves.
2. **One host per request.** The middleware decides the host (`SITE_HOST_HEADER`); pages read it through
   `lib/site/host.ts`. On a non-production host `?site=<market>` shows that market's site.
3. **Fixes found by the review:** /pricing took kroner from a signed-in Norwegian organisation under Empvibe's
   pound template; Sweden's and Germany's pages said en-GB in their JSON-LD; a Swedish or German leader's trial
   mail and a demo link asked for on a Swedish or German page were bokmål (now English, `orgLangOf`); the visit
   counting read DE_SITE and the host overrides in the browser, where they are never set; Swedish and German
   readers saw Norwegian industry names in Oppsett › Selskap; the root description was bokmål in the code.
4. **Packs hold only what differs** (`lib/i18n/merge.ts`, `scripts/i18n/pack-delta.mjs`): 615 copies left out
   (485 in the UK pack). Kept: law texts (`scripts/lib/law.mjs`, shared with legal-pack.test) and the documents
   a market holds whole. Every pack renders as before (`tests/unit/merge.test.ts`).
5. **Source tracking** (`scripts/i18n/stale.mjs`): 21 689 translations record their bokmål; `verify:i18n` fails
   while one is behind. The weekly fold lists them in its pull request instead.
6. **Every site in CI** (`scripts/verify/sites.ts`, the «Every site» step, Germany opened): 56 pages on four
   sites, locally against a production build. ESLint refuses `next/link` in the public site's code.
7. **One brand rule** (`lib/brand-name.ts`) for the app, the mail and the share cards; the support inbox is
   `BRANDS.support`, still hjelp@orgpuls.no for Empvibe until it has a mailbox (Tor's, X-111).

**Deliberately not done:** the Swedish and German site copy stays in their packs (docs/markets/PLAN.md, «One
source for every market»). Prices, VAT and terms for Sweden and Germany wait on SE-E and DE-E: the registry
holds today's values, so each is a data change once decided. `save_billing` still names `'gb'`; a test holds it
to the registry until a migration makes the invoice form a column of `app.markets`.

**Changed for a reader:** Sweden's and Germany's law drawings and articles now carry § (was ✓); their
«Tips ledelsen» links carry `utm_source=skyddsombud` / `betriebsrat`; Swedish and German leaders get their trial
and billing mail in English; the root description on Norway's hosts is the tagline in the reader's language.
